title: Mixed audiences at the Entertainers Club and Beansy's club
summary: The club was Black but whites came as guests with their own tables; Beansy ran it.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What was your story? Was that a place where White and Colored could go or was it?

No, it was a Colored, a nightclub but White used to come in there because Beansley was running the place and he had a lot of White friends and thing and they'd sit them out, you know, certain parts, you know, for themselves. Also the entertainers club. I believe it was, I believe it was Lala the guy that was running the entertainers club.

Yeah, I think so, and I think so, if I ain't got it right. But anyhow, those, in those days and even when when Beansley would run the club behind the old Lyric Theater there, what do they call that? The Elites? Elites, yeah, Elites, yeah. Well, I was a young fellow at the other time. I remember White used to go in those places. They'd go as special guests, you know what I mean? They had their own table and they would feel among themselves because in those days the people of White we wanted to always see the other colored bands and see the colored shows, you know. There was something different from that.
